name: Session boundary gap split
checks: Whether consecutive position timestamps belong to one continuous recording session.
rule: A gap strictly greater than 3600.0 seconds starts a new session.
why: Prevents a shutdown or recording interruption from being treated as continuous motion and from joining unrelated cycle candidates.
discrepancy: No code mismatch. The decision-tree HTML calls the threshold provisional; the current code comment calls it empirically determined. The missing decision-tree Markdown was not present under t1000.

name: Minimum session size
checks: Whether a recording session contains enough complete cycles to represent steady operation.
rule: Proposed N >= 100 complete cycles; N is a placeholder.
why: Would exclude commissioning, aborted, or start-up fragments from a baseline pool.
discrepancy: Documented as a proposed rejection rule, but no corresponding pipeline check was found.

name: Position-based cycle boundary
checks: Whether the position reference signal transitions into and out of the moving state.
rule: moving = position > 1.0; start on <= 1.0 to > 1.0; end on > 1.0 to <= 1.0. Unpaired edge starts are discarded.
why: Segments candidate strokes and avoids emitting incomplete cycles at the end of a detection window.
discrepancy: No threshold mismatch. Both sources use 1.0, but the decision tree presents this as a physical-floor criterion whereas code uses it only for segmentation.

name: Fixed physical duration band
checks: Whether a detected stroke has the expected absolute duration.
rule: Documented proposal: 3.00 <= duration <= 3.20 seconds. Implemented pipeline rule: duration must be > 0 and, when generated, within a run-specific learned median/MAD or 0.01/0.99-quantile bound.
why: Targets partial strokes, merged cycles, standstill, and acquisition failures.
discrepancy: The documented fixed [3.00, 3.20] s physical band is NOT FOUND IN CODE. Code applies positivity plus a learned, dataset-run-specific duration band.

name: Full stroke reached
checks: Whether position traverses the expected full mechanical range.
rule: Documented proposal: maximum_position >= 84.0 AND minimum_position <= 1.0. Implemented pipeline rule: position_stroke_range, if generated, must be within a learned median/MAD or 0.01/0.99-quantile bound.
why: Would exclude incomplete, aborted, or degenerate strokes from a normal-behaviour pool.
discrepancy: The absolute max >= 84.0 and min <= 1.0 rule is NOT FOUND IN CODE. Code validates only learned position_stroke_range bounds, not documented absolute endpoints.

name: Fixed reference-signal sample-count band
checks: Whether the position signal has the expected number of samples within a cycle.
rule: Documented proposal: 60 <= position samples <= 66. Implemented pipeline rule: sample_count and finite_sample_count, when generated, must be within learned median/MAD or 0.01/0.99-quantile bounds.
why: Would flag data loss, duplicated timestamps, or merged cycles.
discrepancy: The fixed 60-66 position-sample band is NOT FOUND IN CODE. Code uses learned bounds for every core signal's sample metrics.

name: In-cycle standstill / frozen segment
checks: Whether motion stops or the position sensor freezes inside an otherwise detected cycle.
rule: Documented proposal: every rolling T window must have position change > delta (suggested delta = 0.5, T = 0.5 s), or motion-phase |velocity| > epsilon. No implemented rolling-window rule exists.
why: Targets a position signal stuck above the segmentation threshold, which can otherwise be emitted as a candidate cycle.
discrepancy: The pipeline computes a whole-cycle constant_signal flag (cycle_quality_profiler.py:120; 135; 142) but does not implement the documented in-cycle rolling standstill rule or reject on that flag.

name: Required signal presence
checks: Whether every signal required for a validation mode is present and non-empty in the cycle interval.
rule: Standalone validation selection checks its configured required_signals for non-empty extraction. Default pipeline dataset validation requires five core signals: position, velocity, current, pressure, temperature. Vibration x/y/z are optional duty-cycled signals; a complete vibration burst yields valid_complete_multisensor_cycle, while absent/partial vibration yields valid_core_cycle if core rules pass.
why: Missing required channels prevent a consistent core record; vibration absence is structurally expected and must not masquerade as a core failure.
implemented: validation_cycle_selection.py:38-72; validation_rule_generation.py:56-60; dataset_validation.py:119-127; dataset_validation.py:266-358; configs/example_pipeline.yaml:36-41; configs/example_pipeline.yaml:60-70
discrepancy: The decision tree says 8/8 signals are required. Current pipeline validation requires five core signals and explicitly treats vibration as optional; the stricter 8/8 interpretation maps only to valid_complete_multisensor_cycle.

name: Configured minimum samples per signal
checks: Whether a signal window has at least its configured minimum sample count for the standalone validation subset.
rule: Configured minima: position 20, velocity 20, current 20, pressure 1, vibration_x/y/z 20, temperature 1. The check applies only to names supplied in required_signals; the example required list contains the five non-vibration core signals.
why: Avoids using almost-empty signal windows as interactive validation examples.
discrepancy: The decision tree describes all eight signals as required. In the example configuration, vibration minima exist but vibration is not in required_validation_signals; this selection utility is not the Stage-10 validation rule.

name: Signal coverage ratio
checks: Whether a signal's first-to-last observed timestamps cover enough of the detected cycle duration.
rule: Documented proposal: position/velocity/current >= 0.95 and pressure >= 0.90; temperature and vibration exempt. Implemented pipeline rule: coverage_ratio is learned per signal from all profiled core cycles, or vibration_complete cycles, using median +/- (3.5 / 0.6745) * MAD; if MAD = 0, use 0.01/0.99 quantiles. Validation enforces only the generated lower bound.
why: Detects a signal clustered in only part of the cycle, leaving a partial dropout hidden by a raw sample count.
implemented: cycle_quality_profiler.py:99-102; cycle_quality_profiler.py:241-247; validation_rule_generation.py:62-72; validation_rule_generation.py:77-86; validation_rule_generation.py:297-358; validation_rule_generation.py:537-564; dataset_validation.py:136-159
discrepancy: The fixed 0.95/0.90 thresholds and stated exemptions are NOT FOUND IN CODE. Code derives per-run learned bounds; optional vibration is handled through availability classes rather than a fixed coverage exemption.

name: Maximum intra-cycle timestamp gap
checks: Whether a signal has an unusually large gap between consecutive samples inside a cycle.
rule: Documented proposal: position/velocity/current/pressure <= 0.15 s, vibration <= 0.10 s, temperature <= 1.5 s. Implemented pipeline rule: maximum_timestamp_gap is learned per signal with median/MAD or 0.01/0.99 quantiles; validation enforces only the generated upper bound.
why: Detects lost measurements during the stroke.
implemented: cycle_quality_profiler.py:60-66; cycle_quality_profiler.py:127; cycle_quality_profiler.py:154; validation_rule_generation.py:77-86; validation_rule_generation.py:297-358; dataset_validation.py:137-159
discrepancy: None of the documented fixed per-signal gap limits is implemented. Code applies learned upper bounds under the downstream metric name maximum_timestamp_gap.

name: Finite values
checks: Whether a required signal has at least one finite numeric value; profiling also counts non-finite samples.
rule: For each core-required signal, finite_sample_count must be > 0. The code does not reject a core signal solely because it contains some non-finite values when at least one finite value remains.
why: Prevents wholly unusable numeric input from reaching validation and feature work.
discrepancy: The decision tree says no signal may contain any NaN or +/- infinity. Code only requires at least one finite value for core signals and does not apply this hard rule to optional vibration.

name: Whole-cycle constant signal
checks: Whether all finite samples in a signal are identical over the complete cycle.
rule: Profiler sets is_constant_signal when finite_value_count > 1 AND std_value == 0.0. It is descriptive only; no direct rejection rule uses this flag. Learned signal_range and standard_deviation rules may be generated, but dataset validation currently evaluates signal_range, not standard_deviation.
why: A constant dynamic signal can indicate a frozen sensor or stuck acquisition buffer.
discrepancy: The decision tree proposes std_value > 0 for dynamic signals as a rejection rule. Code computes the flag, but there is no direct std_value/constant_signal rejection; it only may reject a learned signal_range bound.

name: Invalid position rows removed before segmentation
checks: Whether the position reference row has both a timestamp and a value before candidate-cycle detection.
rule: Drop rows with missing time or value, then sort by time and reset the index.
why: Avoids invalid values corrupting timestamp ordering and movement-edge detection.
discrepancy: Code-only criterion: it is absent from the decision-tree documentation. It is row cleaning, not a per-cycle rejection reason.

name: Cycle interval order
checks: Whether a cycle start timestamp precedes its end timestamp.
rule: Reject when start_time >= end_time or either comparison cannot be parsed.
why: A non-positive or malformed interval cannot represent a real cycle.
discrepancy: Code-only hard rule; the decision tree documents a much stricter fixed duration band instead.

name: Positive cycle duration
checks: Whether the profile reports a strictly positive cycle duration.
rule: Reject when cycle_duration_seconds <= 0; the generated hard-rule record has lower_bound = 0.0.
why: Eliminates zero or negative durations before statistical validation.
discrepancy: Code-only hard minimum. It does not implement the decision tree's 3.00-3.20 s band.

name: Vibration availability class
checks: Whether duty-cycled vibration x/y/z is unavailable, partial, or a complete burst.
rule: Unavailable if total vibration samples = 0. Complete only if every axis exists, has sample_count > 0 and finite_sample_count > 0, and each count is at least 50% of that axis's median non-zero count (minimum 1); otherwise partial.
why: Prevents zero-sample duty-cycled vibration from contaminating vibration thresholds or invalidating otherwise valid core cycles.
discrepancy: Code-only explicit classification. It contradicts the simple decision tree's general statement that missing vibration is rejected; absent/partial vibration produces valid_core_cycle when all core checks pass.

name: Learned signal sampling rate and interval bounds
checks: Whether estimated sampling rate and median sampling interval are typical for a signal in the profiled population.
rule: Rules are generated with median +/- (3.5 / 0.6745) * MAD, or 0.01/0.99 quantiles when MAD = 0, with at least 20 finite reference values. Dataset validation does not currently evaluate these two generated metrics.
why: Would characterize abnormal acquisition cadence, but is not presently an enforced rejection path.
discrepancy: Code generates these rules but the validator's metric loop omits estimated_sampling_rate and median_sampling_interval, so they are not applied. No corresponding decision-tree criterion exists.

name: Consecutive validation-subset block
checks: Whether the optional interactive validation subset consists of adjacent passing cycles within the same session.
rule: When require_consecutive is true, any failed cycle or session change resets the candidate block; selection stops once validation_cycle_count cycles have accumulated. Example config: true, count 3, scan at most 10000.
why: Produces a coherent small subset for interactive validation rather than disconnected passing examples.
discrepancy: Code-only selection policy. It is not part of the default Stage-9/10 dataset-validation path and is absent from the decision tree.

name: Time-gap analysis reporting thresholds
checks: How many consecutive timestamp gaps exceed predefined reporting cutoffs.
rule: Counts gaps strictly greater than 1, 5, 10, 30 seconds; 1, 5, 10, 30 minutes; 1, 6, 24 hours. No cycle/session rejection is made by this module.
why: Provides empirical evidence for selecting and reviewing a session-gap threshold.
discrepancy: Code-only diagnostic criteria. The decision tree states the 3600 s session split but does not document this full reporting threshold set.
